analyzed_vuln.description: `dissect_rtps` inserts the fixed `RTPS_TCPMAP_DOMAIN_ID_KEY_STR` key and an `endpoint_guid` value into `pinfo->private_table`, whose key/value destroy callbacks are `g_free`, but allocates both objects from `wmem_packet_scope()` (`wmem_strdup`/`wmem_memdup`). When the same key is inserted again, `g_hash_table_insert` invokes its destroy callback and directly frees the prior packet-scope `guid_copy` (the allocation shown by ASan; the key has the same ownership mismatch). The pointer remains registered in the wmem packet allocator, so `wmem_leave_packet_scope` later frees it again. Thus the root cause is mixing packet-scope ownership with a GLib hash table that independently frees/replaces entries; the final crash in `wmem_simple_free_all` is only the delayed second free.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: An IPv4/TCP payload must reach the RTPS heuristic dissector and contain a valid non-ping RTPS/RTPX header (supported major version 1 or 2), causing `dissect_rtps` to store the participant GUID in a non-NULL `pinfo->private_table`. The PoV supplies repeated RTPS/RTPX content so `dissect_rtps` performs another insertion of the same constant string key during the same packet scope. GLib frees the previous packet-scope entry during replacement, and leaving packet scope triggers the double-free.

args: Analyze the ownership contract of packet_info::private_table and the insertion in dissect_rtps around line 11942 of wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-rtps.c. How is private_table constructed and destroyed, and should this call use GLib heap allocation (g_strdup/g_memdup2), static keys, replacement, or another API? Identify analogous safe insertions elsewhere in the Wireshark C/C++ source.

The reported ASan crash is a double-free: dissect_rtps puts a wmem_strdup(wmem_packet_scope(), RTPS_TCPMAP_DOMAIN_ID_KEY_STR) key and wmem_memdup(wmem_packet_scope(), &endpoint_guid, sizeof(endpoint_guid)) value into pinfo->private_table. The table reportedly has g_free destroy callbacks. Repeated RTPS content in one packet inserts the constant key again, causing GLib to g_free the prior wmem-managed value, followed by a second free when packet scope ends. We need fix root ownership mismatch in wireshark/epan/dissectors/packet-rtps.c only or related C/C++ source, preserving the mapping functionality.

Does this compile under the project's GLib/C configuration, and does it fully eliminate replacement-time and packet-scope double frees while preserving lookup behavior?

The known reproducer repeatedly invokes dissect_rtps in the same packet and replaces the fixed RTPS_TCPMAP_DOMAIN_ID_KEY_STR entry in pinfo->private_table, which is constructed with g_free destroy callbacks. We applied this exact change: gchar *key = g_strdup(...); endpoint_guid *guid_copy = g_new(endpoint_guid, 1); *guid_copy = guid; g_hash_table_replace(table, key, guid_copy).
